task: Check Java Fast Debug against the accepted C++ interpreter baseline for mixed and fractional numeric comparisons.
observation: A minimal differential probe showed that C++ Fast Debug evaluates `1.9 > 1.1` and `1.1 < 1.9` as true, while Java returned false because its interpreter used integer conversion for relational operators. The Java semantic checker also rejected mixed Int/Float comparisons that the Moss v0.1 guide explicitly permits.
impact: Java Fast Debug now performs floating comparison when either operand is Float, and the checker accepts mixed Int/Float comparisons while retaining rejection for incompatible Bool/Float comparisons. A focused test locks in both fractional and mixed behavior; the direct C++/Java interpreter outputs now match. Full interpreter and native execution parity remain unverified.

resolution.summary: The checker and interpreter agree with documented mixed Int/Float comparison semantics. All eleven Java unit-test classes pass in default and staged ABI-v10 modes; the Java Fast Debug output matches the C++ probe. Full Fast Debug parity and native/Margo integration remain unverified.

task: Verify Java Fast Debug numeric equality against C++ IEEE and mixed-number semantics.
observation: A direct C++/Java probe found Java `Objects.equals` differed on mixed Int/Float equality, signed zero, and NaN: Java reported `2 == 2.0` false, `0.0 == -0.0` false, and NaN equal to itself, while C++ returned the opposite results.
impact: The Java interpreter now compares mixed numeric values after numeric conversion and uses IEEE Float `==`/`!=`, matching Moss behavior. A focused regression covers both operators over mixed Int/Float, signed zero, and NaN. Other interpreter operations remain outside this probe.

resolution.summary: All six focused equality outputs match C++ Fast Debug and all eleven Java unit-test classes pass in ABI-v9. Full Fast Debug/native parity remains unverified.

task: Compare Java and C++ Fast Debug equality for collection-valued expressions.
observation: C++ Fast Debug returned true for `[1] == [1]` and `[1.0] == [1.0]`, while Java returned false because Java collection equality reached `Value` objects that had identity equality only.
impact: Java Fast Debug now compares Vectors and Queues recursively, Maps by matching keys and values, and nominal objects/enums structurally. A focused probe covers nested Int and Float Vectors and matches C++ output. General collection/map edge behavior remains outside the probe.

resolution.summary: Focused scalar, nested Vector, and Float Vector equality outputs match C++ Fast Debug. Clean build and all eleven Java unit-test classes pass in ABI-v9. Full Fast Debug, Map, native, and Margo parity remain unverified.

task: Check Java Fast Debug execution of checked while statements against C++.
observation: The parser and semantic checker accept Moss while loops, but the Java FastInterpreter statement dispatch had no While branch. A checked loop body was therefore visited once as following statements instead of being controlled by the condition.
impact: The interpreter now locates the checked while body and evaluates it repeatedly while the condition remains true. A counter-loop regression compares output with C++ and confirms three iterations. Nested and more complex loop interaction remains outside this probe.

resolution.summary: The Java and C++ Fast Debug counter-loop outputs match, and all eleven Java unit-test classes pass in ABI-v9. Broader while-loop semantics, native behavior, and Margo integration remain unverified.

task: Compare Java Fast Debug local read/write tracing and string values against C++.
observation: A quoted-string trace probe showed Java omitted the local write event, emitted a LocalRead without function/source/identity/line/depth fields, and retained the source escape backslashes in the runtime string. C++ emitted full local events and the decoded string value.
impact: Java now emits local read/write trace events with JSON escaping and source context, and decodes checked Moss string escapes using the parser's canonical escape contract. The bounded local trace probe matches C++ fields and stdout. Other event classes and full trace nesting remain unverified.

resolution.summary: C++ and Java agree on local read/write trace fields and quoted-string output for the focused probe. All eleven Java unit-test classes pass in default ABI-v9 and staged ABI-v10. Broader trace and interpreter parity remain unverified.

task: Compare Java Fast Debug lexical local scopes with C++ for nested branches and loop variables.
observation: A checked probe using `let value = 2` inside an if block printed `2, 2` in Java but `2, 1` in C++ because nested Java blocks reused the parent locals map. A for-loop variable could similarly overwrite a same-named outer binding.
impact: Java now executes nested if/else, while, for, try/recover, and match bodies in scoped locals maps, propagating writes to preexisting names while dropping block declarations and loop bindings. A checked if/for shadowing probe prints `2, 1, 3, 4, 1` in both interpreters. Full ownership, state, and control-flow interpreter parity remain open.

resolution.summary: Java and C++ agree on the focused if/for shadowing output. All eleven Java unit-test classes pass in default ABI-v9 and staged ABI-v10; broader interpreter parity and native/Margo integration remain unverified.

task: Check Fast Debug recovery payload binding and lexical lifetime against C++.
observation: A checked `Failure.Bad(code: 2)` probe showed Java bound the whole enum value to the recover pattern name and left it in the parent locals map. C++ binds the named payload value only within the recovery arm and restores the outer local afterward.
impact: Java now extracts the named enum payload field (or the single payload field for positional compatibility), scopes the recovery binding, and restores a shadowed outer binding. The regression prints `2` inside recovery and `1` afterward, matching C++. Other multi-payload and nested recovery cases remain unverified.

resolution.summary: Focused recovery payload and scope output match between C++ and Java; all eleven unit-test classes pass in ABI-v9 and staged ABI-v10. Broader recovery parity remains unverified.

task: Compare Java Fast Debug loop traces with C++ event-for-event for a checked while loop.
observation: The checked while trace initially lacked Java LoopIteration events, nested body depth and parent/control IDs, reassignment before values, and correct source lines on condition reads after the first iteration.
impact: Java now emits iteration events, nests local events beneath each loop iteration, records local write before/after values, and resets trace source context for each condition evaluation. The focused while-loop trace JSON objects and stdout now compare equal to C++. Other trace constructs remain unverified.

resolution.summary: All event objects and stdout from the focused C++/Java while trace match; all eleven Java unit-test classes pass in ABI-v9 and staged ABI-v10. Branch, for, message, state, and full trace parity remain open.

task: Compare Java Fast Debug range-for trace events with C++.
observation: After while-loop trace support, a range-for probe still showed Java omitted both LoopIteration events and the nested parent/control event context, although stdout matched.
impact: Java for loops now emit numbered LoopIteration events and run each checked body at nested depth under the iteration control event. A complete range(0, 2) trace and stdout match C++ exactly. Vector/Map iteration trace behavior remains unverified.

resolution.summary: The complete range-for trace and stdout match between C++ and Java; all eleven Java test classes pass in ABI-v9 and staged ABI-v10. Vector/Map and other trace constructs remain open.

task: Compare Java Fast Debug branch tracing for selected then and else arms against C++.
observation: After loop control-event tracing was added, an if/else probe still showed Java omitted the C++ BranchTaken event and emitted branch-body reads at the parent depth without control-event links.
impact: Java now emits BranchTaken events for selected then/else arms and nests branch body events under the control event with incremented depth. A two-branch probe matches C++ trace JSON objects and stdout exactly. Other control, message, and state traces remain unverified.

resolution.summary: C++ and Java branch trace JSON objects and stdout match for both then and else selection; all eleven Java test classes pass in ABI-v9 and staged ABI-v10. Broader trace parity remains open.

task: Compare direct function-call trace events between Java Fast Debug and C++.
observation: A checked helper-call probe showed Java omitted function entry, return, and exit events and did not carry call-event context into the callee local read. C++ emitted four events with stable function identity and nested depth.
impact: Java now emits FunctionEnter, explicit or implicit Return, and FunctionExit for direct source function calls, and includes the active call event ID in nested trace context. The minimal add_one probe's complete trace and stdout match C++ exactly; pipeline callback and method trace paths remain unverified.

resolution.summary: Focused direct-call trace JSON objects and stdout match between C++ and Java, and Java unit tests pass in ABI-v9 and staged ABI-v10. Other call forms and error-path traces remain unverified.

task: Compare Java and C++ trace summaries for local Vector values and range-for iteration.
observation: A Vector range-for trace matched control and local-access events, but the initial LocalWrite detail showed Java's element list while C++ reported a compact collection-size summary.
impact: Java local trace writes now use compact collection summaries consistent with C++ (`Vector(size=n)`, `Queue(size=n)`, `Map(size=n)`) and object type names. The full Vector loop trace and stdout match C++ for the focused probe; other collection and state-event shapes remain unverified.

resolution.summary: Complete Vector range-for trace JSON and stdout compare equal between C++ and Java; all eleven Java test classes pass in ABI-v9 and staged ABI-v10.

task: Compare typed raise/recover trace events and semantic identity in Java Fast Debug against C++.
observation: A typed `Failure.Bad(code: 2)` probe showed Java omitted both `raise` and `recover` trace events and labeled main as `main@1` despite its declaration on line 3.
impact: Java now emits raise/recover events with canonical enum identity and derives main semantic identity from its declaration line. The complete typed recovery trace and stdout match C++ exactly; other error variants and nested recovery traces remain unverified.

resolution.summary: Focused typed raise/recover trace and stdout match byte-for-byte between C++ and Java; all eleven Java unit-test classes pass in ABI-v9 and staged ABI-v10.

task: Compare Java object method trace lifecycle and receiver access against C++ Fast Debug.
observation: A checked `Box.get()` probe showed Java emitted no method lifecycle events and skipped the local receiver read, while C++ recorded receiver access followed by MethodEnter, nested field read, Return, and MethodExit.
impact: Java now records receiver LocalRead and emits method lifecycle events with owner-qualified identity and nested call context for interpreted object methods. The focused method trace and stdout match C++; other receiver forms, mutation methods, and exceptional exits remain unverified.

resolution.summary: Complete direct object method trace and stdout match between C++ and Java; all eleven Java unit-test classes pass in ABI-v9 and staged ABI-v10.

task: Verify Fast Debug call trace context unwinds correctly when a helper raises into a recover arm.
observation: The checked helper-raise/recover probe preserves the callee's nested raise event, then restores main identity and depth for the recovery event without emitting a false FunctionExit.
impact: An exact event-sequence Java unit regression now protects exceptional call unwinding and trace context restoration. This is focused trace evidence and does not establish general exception semantics or full Fast Debug parity.

resolution.summary: Focused C++ and Java exceptional call trace JSON and stdout match; all eleven Java unit-test classes pass in ABI-v9 and staged ABI-v10.

task: Classify Java and C++ diagnostics for a typed Map used as a for-loop iterable.
observation: Both compilers rejected `for key in values` when values was an inferred `Map[String, Int]`, but Java reported an unresolved loop variable at line 1 while C++ reported that the Map was not statically iterable at the loop line.
impact: Java now rejects Map iteration directly at the loop with a non-iterable type diagnostic, preventing the unrelated open-result inference error. Vector/range iteration remains unchanged; broader iterator acceptance is not covered by this correction.

resolution.summary: Java reports TYPE_MISMATCH at the same loop line with the non-iterable Map explanation; both Java unit suite runs pass.

task: Compare checked Queue iteration acceptance and diagnostics across Java and C++.
observation: A typed Queue loop was rejected by C++ as non-iterable but Java reached unresolved loop-variable inference. The same early classification issue as Map iteration existed for Queue.
impact: The Java checker now rejects both Map and Queue at the loop source with an explicit non-iterable diagnostic. This prevents the misleading open-result error; accepted Vector/range cases are unaffected by the targeted guard.

resolution.summary: Java now reports TYPE_MISMATCH at the Queue loop line with the non-iterable explanation; all eleven unit-test classes pass in ABI-v9 and staged ABI-v10.

task: Compare domain construction trace metadata between Java and C++ Fast Debug.
observation: A domain/message trace showed Java's domain_instance event used the domain declaration line and omitted source and semantic identity; it also emitted a LocalWrite containing the Java DomainInstance object address.
impact: Java domain_instance events now use the active Moss source location and main semantic identity, include the domain specialization, and domain handles no longer produce opaque LocalWrite summaries. The initial domain construction event matches C++; remaining message and state events on the same probe still diverge and are not claimed fixed.

resolution.summary: Focused domain construction event matches C++ exactly; all eleven Java unit-test classes pass in ABI-v9 and staged ABI-v10. Message/state trace parity remains open.

task: Compare domain message, handler, state, and reply trace context against C++ Fast Debug.
observation: The `domains_and_messages.moss` trace exposed missing message/handler event-stack IDs, handler semantic identity, state access metadata, reply events, and the LocalWrite for a message result. Domain handles also appeared as opaque Java object strings.
impact: Java now carries message and handler nesting through event IDs, emits structured state reads/writes and reply context, records message result writes, and omits domain handle object strings. The full trace and stdout for this example now compare byte-for-byte with C++; nested/cross-domain routes and failure handlers remain unverified.

resolution.summary: Complete trace JSON and stdout for the focused Worker Run/Get example compare byte-for-byte; all eleven Java unit-test classes pass in ABI-v9 and staged ABI-v10.

task: Compare nested direct calls and object payload messages inside a domain handler against C++ Fast Debug tracing.
observation: The `phase2_safety.moss` trace showed Java adding local reads for simple direct-call arguments, using depth 1 for helper bodies nested inside handlers, and expanding an object message detail while C++ used its nominal summary.
impact: Java now avoids a duplicate read for a simple local passed to a source callable, derives nested body depth from the active event stack, emits inherited domain context on nested function lifecycle events, and uses Moss value summaries for message details and returns. The full phase2_safety trace and stdout now match C++; other nested domain and ownership cases remain unverified.

resolution.summary: Complete trace JSON and stdout for phase2_safety.moss match byte-for-byte; all eleven Java unit-test classes pass in ABI-v9 and staged ABI-v10.

task: Compare named domain state construction and statically routed nested messages against C++.
observation: A two-hop Ledger→Inventory route showed Java ignored `Ledger(balance: 42)` and retained the declaration default 10, while C++ preserved 42. The same probe exposed synthesized message expression statements losing caller source and nested event-stack context.
impact: Java domain construction now binds named arguments to declared state fields as well as declared routes and avoids tracing route-handle arguments as local reads. Synthesized message statements inherit the active source, line, function, and depth. The phase106b static composition example now returns 42, and its complete trace matches C++; broader router/state initialization profiles remain open.

resolution.summary: Named domain state and two-hop route behavior now return 42; complete trace and stdout for phase106b_static_composition compare byte-for-byte. All eleven Java unit-test classes pass in ABI-v9 and staged ABI-v10.

task: Trace a bare Moss pipeline function stage through Java Fast Debug's normal function lifecycle.
observation: Java executes a bare `value |> twice` stage, but the pipeline path called the function body directly and skipped normal function trace events. The C++ Fast Debug reports this stage as unsupported, so it cannot serve as a trace oracle for this Java-supported form.
impact: Java now invokes bare pipeline stages through the normal function-call path, preserving call entry/return/exit events and semantic identity. A focused regression checks the computed result and lifecycle trace; this verifies Java behavior but does not claim C++ Fast Debug parity for bare stages.

resolution.summary: Java bare pipeline stage computes the expected value and emits function lifecycle events; all eleven unit-test classes pass in ABI-v9 and staged ABI-v10. C++ interpreter reports the pipeline stage unsupported.

task: Compare repeated nested state-changing messages and local assignment trace ordering against C++.
observation: The `shared_memory.moss` probe matched output and event nesting, but Java serialized domain instance/specialization/handler context after LocalWrite's after-value; C++ emits domain context before before/after values.
impact: Java now places inherited domain metadata in the canonical trace field order for local writes. The complete shared_memory trace and stdout match C++ byte-for-byte, covering repeated message state changes and handler-local result writes.

resolution.summary: Full shared_memory trace and stdout match byte-for-byte; all eleven Java unit-test classes pass in ABI-v9 and staged ABI-v10.

task: Compare inferred generic function specialization metadata in Fast Debug call traces.
observation: The `domain_typing.moss` trace matched execution and event order, but Java omitted C++'s `fn:twice<int>@2` specialization identity on function lifecycle and local events.
impact: Java now selects the matching checked function specialization from runtime argument types and emits its semantic identity on trace events; explicitly typed nongeneric functions do not gain a spurious specialization field. The full domain_typing trace now matches C++ exactly.

resolution.summary: Complete domain_typing trace and stdout compare byte-for-byte; all eleven Java unit-test classes pass in ABI-v9 and staged ABI-v10.

task: Validate Fast Debug on_fail pattern dispatch and checker-approved captures across try/recover control flow.
observation: The Java Fast Interpreter selected the first on_fail arm unconditionally and did not restore checked captures after try/recover scopes. The phase21_capture_try_join.moss fixture returned () twice, while C++ returned no and yes.
impact: Java now selects the matching arm, transports exceptional-edge locals, and retains names joined across try/recover alternatives. The focused result is no then yes; on_fail traces identify the failure arm and captured local. Whole-trace comparison still shows unrelated branch context/event differences.

resolution.summary: Focused Java execution now returns no and yes, with matching on_fail captured-read and reply values; all eleven Java unit-test classes pass in ABI-v9 and staged ABI-v10. Full trace parity is not claimed.

task: Exercise multiple typed on_fail arms with enum payload bindings in Java Fast Debug.
observation: The multiple-arm fixture selected the right error arm after dispatch was corrected, but payload names are encoded in patterns like Failure.First(code), while FailureArm.binding remains empty. Java printed first () and second ().
impact: Java extracts the selected pattern payload binding and exposes the raised enum payload to the failure body. Both typed arms now produce the same output as C++.

resolution.summary: Java prints first 7 then second 9, matching C++; all eleven Java unit-test classes pass in ABI-v9 and staged ABI-v10.

task: Check Java Fast Debug capture visibility for locals joined across if/else branches.
observation: The phase21_capture_if_join.moss fixture declares the same local on both branches and raises afterward. C++ returns the corresponding value through on_fail, while Java returned unit for both branch choices.
impact: Java now preserves the selected branch value for names declared in both sides of an if/else and the fixture produces yes then no, matching C++. A separate method-raise fixture exposed an unrelated Java ownership checker rejection and remains open.

resolution.summary: If-join capture output matches C++ and all eleven Java unit-test classes pass in ABI-v9 and staged ABI-v10. Separate ownership parity finding remains open.

task: Compare Java ownership checking for a consuming call whose first argument raises before later arguments are evaluated.
observation: C++ accepts phase21_capture_method_early_raise.moss, while Java reports OWNERSHIP_USE_AFTER_CONSUME for data in on_fail. The first argument fail() raises before consume_after can receive the later data argument, so Java appears to apply the normal-path move to the failure edge.
impact: This is an unresolved Java ownership exceptional-edge parity gap. Correct support likely requires snapshots at potentially raising call-argument evaluation points; no code change is made pending a narrow design and regression.

resolution.summary: C++ check accepts; Java check rejects at the on_fail capture with OWNERSHIP_USE_AFTER_CONSUME. Focused investigation remains.

task: Compare Java checking and execution for owned match-case payload capture in on_fail.
observation: C++ accepts and executes phase21_capture_owned_payload.moss, returning hello; Java rejects the on_fail use of match binder value as UNKNOWN_SYMBOL_OR_TYPE. The borrowed payload counterpart is rejected by C++ as ON_FAIL_CAPTURE_NOT_OWNED, while Java reports the unknown name first.
impact: The Java checker does not expose match-case payload bindings as typed exceptional-edge captures in on_fail, and the current error masks the ownership-specific rejection for borrowed payloads. This remains an open semantic parity gap.

resolution.summary: Owned case returns hello only in C++; borrowed case is rejected by C++ with ON_FAIL_CAPTURE_NOT_OWNED; Java currently rejects both with unknown identifier value.

task: Support checker-proved on_fail capture of an owned match-consume payload.
observation: An owned payload binder introduced by match consume existed on explicit raise snapshots, but Java removed the binder from the enclosing handler environment before checking on_fail.
impact: The checker now exposes consumed match-case binders to failure-arm checking and validates them on selected raise edges. The owned payload fixture returns hello in both C++ and Java, and SemanticCheckerTest asserts the checked capture. The borrowed counterpart remains rejected by Java with a generic unknown-name diagnostic rather than C++ ON_FAIL_CAPTURE_NOT_OWNED.

resolution.summary: Owned capture returns hello in both compilers and a Java semantic regression asserts the edge capture. Borrowed capture still rejects but diagnostic specificity differs.

task: Report the ownership-specific diagnostic for borrowed match payloads used as on_fail captures.
observation: After allowing match payload binders in failure-arm checking, Java initially accepted a borrowed payload, which exposed that the checker needed to distinguish match from match consume.
impact: The checker now rejects the borrowed capture with ON_FAIL_CAPTURE_NOT_OWNED, matching C++ behavior. Tests cover the valid consumed capture and invalid borrowed capture.

resolution.summary: Java rejects the borrowed capture with ON_FAIL_CAPTURE_NOT_OWNED, while the consumed-payload positive fixture succeeds; all eleven unit-test classes pass in ABI-v9 and staged ABI-v10.

task: Preserve pre-transfer ownership state when a helper raises during evaluation of a call argument.
observation: The checker marked a later owned argument consumed on every path before accounting for an earlier argument call that raises. It also checked on_fail bodies against the normal-path environment instead of the selected exceptional edge.
impact: Java now records ownership snapshots for direct helper raises found inside call arguments before normal-path moves and checks failure arms against selected edge state. The method early-raise fixture checks and executes in Java, returning 3 like C++; existing consumed capture fixtures still reject with ON_FAIL_CAPTURE_CONSUMED. Indirect raise-effect summaries and broader argument sequencing remain unverified.

resolution.summary: Direct raising-argument fixture matches C++ output 3; consumed capture fixtures reject in both compilers with ON_FAIL_CAPTURE_CONSUMED; all Java test classes pass in ABI-v9 and staged ABI-v10.

task: Reject ambiguous on_fail capture names that refer to distinct local bindings on separate raise edges.
observation: The C++ checker rejects an on_fail capture when same-named locals are separately declared in two selected branches. Java previously merged by name and accepted the capture.
impact: Java now compares local binding declaration lines on selected raise snapshots and rejects the mismatched capture with ON_FAIL_CAPTURE_BINDING_MISMATCH.

resolution.summary: C++ and Java both reject with ON_FAIL_CAPTURE_BINDING_MISMATCH; Java test suites pass in ABI-v9 and staged ABI-v10.

task: Prevent ownership transfer of domain state into handler locals.
observation: C++ rejects consuming a transfer-typed domain state field into a local, while Java marked the field moved and accepted the handler.
impact: Java now rejects domain state consumption with MOSS_COMPILE_ERROR, matching C++ for the state-borrow fixture.

resolution.summary: C++ and Java both reject domain-state consumption with MOSS_COMPILE_ERROR.

task: Restore availability of a mutable local after assigning a fresh value following ownership transfer.
observation: The Java ownership environment retained the consumed flag after a mutable local was assigned a fresh value, causing a false ON_FAIL_CAPTURE_CONSUMED in a loop fixture accepted by C++.
impact: A new assignment now clears the target local consumed state before recording RHS transfers. The loop reinitialization fixture is accepted and returns after in both interpreters; consumed-edge fixtures continue to reject with ON_FAIL_CAPTURE_CONSUMED.

resolution.summary: Loop reinitialization acceptance and output match C++; consumed-capture diagnostic also matches C++; all Java suites pass in both ABI modes.

task: Match nested domain raise propagation into a caller handler try/recover before selecting inner on_fail.
observation: On a nested call, Java selected the inner domain on_fail immediately and returned 8 to the caller, while C++ propagated the raise to the enclosing handler recover and returned 9. A direct call from main still correctly selects the inner on_fail.
impact: Java now defers nested handler failure-arm dispatch so the caller handler can recover the synchronous message failure. The direct and nested outputs are 8 and 9, matching C++; a FastInterpreterTest covers the sequence.

resolution.summary: Focused fixture now prints 8 then 9 in C++ and Java; all eleven Java unit-test classes pass in ABI-v9 and staged ABI-v10.

task: Prevent literal dead-branch ownership effects from contaminating reachable recovery paths.
observation: The C++ checker accepted phase21_capture_slot_combined.moss, but Java propagated a move from an if false branch into recovery checking and rejected a later read on a reachable different error path.
impact: Java now uses literal true/false conditions to select the reachable ownership environment after checking both alternatives. The combined capture fixture is accepted and returns seven in both interpreters; a semantic regression covers dead-branch ownership isolation.

resolution.summary: Fixture now checks and returns seven in both compilers; all Java unit-test classes pass in ABI-v9 and staged ABI-v10.

task: Restore caller trace context when a nested domain raise propagates into an outer recover.
observation: After nested raise propagation was corrected, the outer recover trace retained the inner handler semantic identity and parent IDs because the propagating message did not unwind its trace stacks.
impact: Java now unwinds the nested handler/message trace context without emitting normal handler exit or message return events. The complete output and trace for phase21_on_fail_root_nested.moss compare byte-for-byte with C++; a unit test asserts the outer handler identity on recovery.

resolution.summary: Complete output and trace match C++ byte-for-byte for the nested failure fixture; all Java unit-test classes pass in ABI-v9 and staged ABI-v10.

task: Prevent loop-local bindings and unreachable zero-iteration raises from becoming handler captures.
observation: A focused capture-family check found Java accepted phase21_capture_loop_uninit.moss, while C++ rejected it because a let inside while false was not initialized on the later raise edge. Java had allowed loop-body declarations and dead-branch raise snapshots to leak.
impact: Java now checks while bodies in a copied scope, merges ownership effects only for bindings present before a potentially executing loop, and discards raise snapshots from literal while false. The uninitialized fixture rejects with ON_FAIL_CAPTURE_NOT_INITIALIZED, while loop-reinit and loop-consumed controls also match C++.

resolution.summary: Loop-uninitialized, loop-reinit, and loop-consumed checker outcomes match C++; both Java unit suite runs pass.

task: Compare basic on_fail checker contracts for ambiguity, variant coverage, escaping errors, and handler replies.
observation: The phase21_on_fail fixture sweep showed four Java false accepts: ambiguous untyped binding across error enums, missing variant coverage, a direct raise escaping an on_fail arm, and a missing reply from a value-returning handler.
impact: Java now rejects these simple direct cases with AMBIGUOUS_RECOVERY_BINDING, NONEXHAUSTIVE_ON_FAIL, ON_FAIL_MUST_HANDLE_ERRORS, and ON_FAIL_REPLY_REQUIRED respectively, matching C++. Exhaustiveness checks are skipped when a handler body contains try because escaping-edge analysis is not complete. The recovery_semantics fixture remains a Java-only rejection because a plain recover err binder lacks an inferred enum type for match.

resolution.summary: Four direct on_fail rejection cases now match C++ codes; nested try exhaustiveness is intentionally not claimed. Plain recover binding type inference remains open. All Java test classes pass in ABI-v9 and staged ABI-v10.

task: Type and execute a plain catch-all recover binding when the try body raises one known enum type.
observation: The Java checker did not assign a type to `recover err`, so a following exhaustive match on the raised enum failed with UNKNOWN_SYMBOL_OR_TYPE; the interpreter also treated the identifier as a variant selector instead of a catch-all binding.
impact: Java now infers the enum type from directly visible raises and helper-call raise bodies, binds the raised enum value in catch-all recovery, and avoids unreachable warnings for the binding form. phase21_recovery_semantics now matches C++ stdout and warning diagnostics; FastInterpreterTest checks recovery binding plus exhaustive match. Mixed-enum/indirect raise summaries remain outside this bounded fix.

resolution.summary: Recovery fixture output and unreachable-variant diagnostics match C++; all seven targeted on_fail/recovery check fixtures align; all Java unit classes pass in ABI-v9 and staged ABI-v10.

task: Dispatch typed failure arms by full enum identity when distinct error enums reuse a variant name.
observation: A two-error-enum probe with FirstError.Bad and SecondError.Bad was accepted by both compilers, but Java matched by the short `.Bad` suffix and executed the first on_fail arm for both raises.
impact: Java now compares the qualified raised enum and variant against the qualified arm selector, normalizing module separators. The output is first then second, matching C++; a FastInterpreterTest covers the collision.

resolution.summary: Distinct qualified arms dispatch correctly and match C++; all Java unit-test classes pass in ABI-v9 and staged ABI-v10.

task: Check all branches of on_fail bodies for required replies and directly escaping raises.
observation: The simple on_fail checks only detected a direct raise and accepted a value-returning arm if any nested branch replied. C++ requires all branches to reply and rejects raises escaping from a branch.
impact: Java now walks basic if/else structure to require reply on every value-returning path and rejects branch-contained raises if no nested try exists. Two semantic unit tests cover the cases; both diagnostic codes match C++. Nested try escaping-flow analysis remains limited.

resolution.summary: Both branch-focused diagnostics match C++; all Java test classes pass in ABI-v9 and staged ABI-v10.

task: Emit structured branch trace events for selected enum match cases during recovery.
observation: The phase21_recovery_semantics output matched across interpreters, but Java omitted the BranchTaken event for match err after recover err, leaving a trace-only divergence.
impact: Java now emits BranchTaken at the selected Case source line and scopes the control event to the selected case body. Complete stdout and trace for the recovery/reraise fixture now compare byte-for-byte with C++; the catch-all recovery unit test asserts the branch event.

resolution.summary: Complete recovery fixture stdout and trace compare byte-for-byte with C++; both ABI Java test runs pass.

task: Preserve active domain context on Fast Debug control-flow trace events.
observation: A nine-file failure-capture trace sample showed BranchTaken and LoopIteration events lacked the same instance, specialization, and handler metadata carried by neighboring events.
impact: Control events now use the shared domain context helper. The five previously exact traces remain exact and stdout matches in all nine fixtures. Four other traces still differ in localized event emission or rendering details; this is not a full trace parity claim.

resolution.summary: Domain context appears on control events and both ABI-mode Java suites pass; remaining trace differences are documented without claiming full parity.

task: Trace the selected implicit else path and close its control scope in Fast Debug.
observation: For an if without an explicit else, the false path executed but Java omitted BranchTaken while C++ emitted an else branch event. A first fix revealed that an unclosed event scope also contaminated following on_fail event context.
impact: Java now emits the implicit else event and immediately closes the control scope. The complete phase21_capture_try_join fixture stdout and trace compare byte-for-byte with C++. A refreshed eight-fixture subset has matching acceptance and stdout throughout; three other full-trace differences remain localized and are not being represented as semantic parity failures.

resolution.summary: Implicit else selection is traced, its control context is popped, and the focused fixture trace matches C++; both ABI Java suites pass.

task: Prevent ownership consumption in a provably unreachable recover arm from contaminating reachable code.
observation: A 91-file checker screen found a Java-only rejection where a direct raise of Failure.A made a Failure.B recover arm unreachable, but a consume in that arm marked a local consumed after the reachable Failure.A arm.
impact: For payload-free recover patterns and try bodies consisting only of direct raises, Java checks the unreachable body in an isolated ownership environment and discards its flow effects. The affected fixture is accepted by both compilers with RECOVER_UNREACHABLE_VARIANT preserved. The broad screen's acceptance mismatches decreased from 18 to 17; other paths remain conservative.

resolution.summary: Focused false rejection is corrected; the unreachable variant warning remains, and both ABI Java suites pass. The wider fixture screen still has 17 acceptance mismatches.

task: Reject bare raise outside an active recover arm in the Java semantic checker.
observation: The 91-file acceptance screen found Java accepted phase21_bare_raise_invalid.moss, where a function issues bare raise without a recover binding; C++ reports BARE_RAISE_OUTSIDE_RECOVER.
impact: Java now tracks recover scope across nested checker blocks and emits BARE_RAISE_OUTSIDE_RECOVER for bare raises outside the scope. Tests cover invalid bare raise and valid reraising inside recover. The refreshed 91-file screen now reports 8 C++-only and 8 Java-only acceptance mismatches, with 53 both accepted and 22 both rejected.

resolution.summary: Bare raise scope matches the C++ rejection rule in the focused fixture; both ABI Java suites pass and the broad screen has 16 remaining acceptance mismatches.

task: Reject root message ingress when its statically known handler can raise without exhaustive on_fail handling.
observation: The 91-fixture screen exposed Java-only acceptance of typed raises escaping executor roots and synchronous root messages, including nested helper calls and a call in a return expression.
impact: Java now resolves executor submissions and synchronous main-level root message sites to handlers and follows statically named function calls to collect direct raises. Three false accepts now reject with ROOT_UNHANDLED_RAISE, while the handled executor root fixture remains accepted. Root handlers containing local try/recover or failure arms remain outside this bounded check. The 91-file screen falls to 10 acceptance mismatches (8 C++-only, 2 Java-only).

resolution.summary: Three focused root-ingress false accepts are corrected; valid exhaustive on_fail root remains accepted and both ABI Java suites pass.

task: Assess ownership and failure-edge ordering within vector literals.
observation: A vector literal containing a consume before a later raising element is a Java-only false accept. A trial left-to-right ownership traversal caught it but also falsely rejected the paired case where the raising element precedes the consume, because recover checking still uses the post-assignment environment instead of selected raise-edge state.
impact: The trial code and regression were reverted before checkpointing. No behavior regressed in the working tree. Correct handling requires try/recover edge-state selection that preserves both ordering cases; the 91-file acceptance screen remains 8 C++-only and 2 Java-only mismatches.

resolution.summary: Deferred the vector fix because normal-path literal traversal alone regressed the paired exceptional-edge control; explicit recover-edge ownership remains needed.

task: Preserve ownership at each raising stage in functional pipelines that share a recover variant.
observation: phase21_pipeline_shared_variant_edges.moss is a Java-only false accept. Its paired positive proves source(flag) may raise before reduce consumes data, while fold may raise after the consume; both edges use the same recover variant and recovery must be valid on both.
impact: The C++ checker records callback failure at the pipeline stage boundary. Java currently does not model these stage-specific exceptional ownership states. A partial source-order-only fix risks rejecting phase21_pipeline_source_before_consume.moss, so no code change was kept. The 91-file checker sample remains 8 C++-only and 2 Java-only mismatches.

resolution.summary: Stage-specific pipeline exceptional ownership remains open; no partial fix was retained because the source-before-consume positive must remain accepted.

task: Select recovery ownership from ordered exceptional edges across call arguments, vector literals, and reduce stages.
observation: Paired acceptance fixtures showed the same recover variant can arise before or after a local is transferred. Post-assignment state rejected early-raise positives and accepted later-raise negatives; normal-path-only literal traversal also regressed the paired vector order.
impact: Java now checks recovery bodies against matching raise snapshots and merges those paths with normal completion. Call arguments and vector elements are traversed left-to-right; reduce source, initializer transfer, and callback edges are recorded in stage order. Same-variant edges are retained together. A catch-all on_fail is recognized as exhaustive. All four paired ownership groups align; the 91-file screen is now 7 C++-only, 0 Java-only (54 both accept, 30 both reject). Both ABI Java suites pass.

resolution.summary: Focused call/vector/pipeline recovery edge pairs and catch-all on_fail pass; ABI-v9/v10 suites pass and the 91-file acceptance screen has no Java-only accepts.

task: Infer catch-all recovery enum type through a scalar function call that may raise.
observation: phase21_peer_raise_scalar_call.moss raises the Int result of number(fail), where number conditionally raises Failure.Bad. Java previously mistook the call expression for an enum variant, failed to type recover err, and warned that Failure.Bad was unreachable.
impact: Raised-enum summaries now follow statically named functions nested in raise and result expressions. The fixture is accepted without spurious recovery warnings, matching C++. A focused semantic test covers catch-all binding through the scalar call. The 91-file checker sample improves to 6 C++-only and 0 Java-only acceptance differences; both ABI Java suites pass.

resolution.summary: Scalar-call raised enum inference matches the fixture; both ABI Java suites pass and the 91-file screen has no Java-only accepts.

task: Align Range indexing and ownership snapshots for try/recover in ordinary functions and main.
observation: The acceptance screen found a valid Range byte index rejected by Java and a valid recovery arm falsely rejected after an owned value had been consumed on the normal path, although the selected failure edge retained it.
impact: Expression typing now accepts Range[Int] indexing as Int. Raise snapshots are now collected for try/recover in ordinary functions and main as well as handlers, and recovery checks use matching exceptional ownership edges. The Range fixture and string recovery fixture now pass; the 91-file screen improves to 4 C++-only, 0 Java-only, 57 both accepted, 30 both rejected. Both ABI Java suites pass all 11 classes.

resolution.summary: Both focused fixtures and both ABI Java suites pass; the updated bounded checker screen has no Java-only acceptance mismatches.

task: Restore an outer binding after a shadowing For loop without breaking loop-body typing.
observation: phase21_peer_speculation.moss shows Java retains the iteration variable's Int type after `for chunk in [1]`, where the outer binding is Range; the following byte index is rejected. A general For body-scope rewrite made this fixture pass but caused the existing object-method loop argument test to lose its `key` binder.
impact: The attempted rewrite was reverted, preserving prior behavior. Rebuilt source passes the ABI-v9 and staged ABI-v10 Java suites. No loop fix is claimed; the remaining 91-fixture screen has this one non-FileIO acceptance divergence plus the typed-raising iterator limitation and FileIO cases.

resolution.summary: A correct fix needs to preserve loop-body binder visibility and restore only the shadowed outer name after the loop; the broad control-flow rewrite was removed.
